help: The model's estimated chance that the bet wins, from its own inputs (team ratings for game markets, the player's recent distribution for props). For spreads, totals and props a separate push probability is kept.
1 / decimal price. It includes the book's margin (vig), so the two sides of a market add up to more than 100%.
The book's two-sided prices rescaled so they add up to 100%. Shown only when both sides were quoted. It is the market's estimate without the margin.
EV per 1 unit staked = p × (d − 1) − (1 − p), where p is the model probability and d the decimal price. When a push is possible, the push probability returns the stake and is left out of both terms.
The lowest decimal price at which EV still clears the market's EV threshold. A price shorter than this is not worth taking under the model.
A push (the result lands exactly on the line) or a void (player did not play, game cancelled) returns the stake: zero units, counted apart from wins and losses.
'conservative' means the book did not label which side each price belonged to; the worse of the two prices was used, so EV and ROI are lower bounds.
+EV is a theoretical expectation under the model, not a guarantee. It is only as good as the model's probability, which has not yet passed its validation gates.
